newsitem.title: USA: New Calif. auto insurance plan clears final hurdle.
newsitem.headline: New Calif. auto insurance plan clears final hurdle.

text.p: A new system for determining automobile insurance rates in California has received final approval, paving the way for the regulations to take effect in early 1997, state officials said on Monday.

The California Department of Insurance said automobile insurance companies will have until February 1997 to comply with the regulations, which require that auto insurance rates be based primarily on a driver's safety record, miles driven annually and years of driving experience.

The state Office of Administrative Law initially approved the new automobile insurance system last July, but asked the Department of Insurance to clarify one subsection of the rules outlining how good driver discounts are calculated.
That subsection has now been approved, allowing the Insurance Department to set an implementation date for the new rules. The deadline for implementation will be February 17.
"Its been a long time coming, but rules are now finalized," California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said.
